name: SceneNet
description: We introduce SceneNet, a framework for generating high-quality annotated 3D scenes to aid indoor scene understanding. SceneNet leverages manually-annotated datasets of real world scenes such as NYUv2 to learn statistics about object co-occurrences and their spatial relationships. Using a hierarchical simulated annealing optimisation, these statistics are exploited to generate a potentially unlimited number of new annotated scenes, by sampling objects from various existing databases of 3D objects such as ModelNet, and textures such as OpenSurfaces and ArchiveTextures. Depending on the task, SceneNet can be used directly in the form of annotated 3D models for supervised training and 3D reconstruction benchmarking, or in the form of rendered annotated sequences of RGB-D frames or videos.
general_score_metric: mean_iou (for semantic segmentation tasks; other tasks use mAP or RMSE)
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on synthetic 3D indoor scenes. Major caveats: synthetic-to-real domain gap (sim2real), task-dependent metrics, and potential dataset/model bias from object/model repositories used to populate scenes.
